title: Coin Combinations II

constraints.text: n ≤ 100 coins, x ≤ 1e6, unordered ways, mod 1e9+7

explanation: Unordered ways: process coin types one at a time, so each multiset is built in a fixed order and counted once.
traps: Using sum-outer loops counts permutations instead (Coin Combinations I).

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[i][s] = number of ways to make s using only the first i coin types (rolled into dp[s])
dp[s] = number of ordered sequences summing to s
options.why: Counts 2+3 and 3+2 separately — that's Coin Combinations I.
Works only if you also force non-decreasing order; much bigger than needed.

options.text: dp[i][s] = 1 if coin i is used in sum s

extraLayers.explanation: Fixing the order in which coin types are considered makes each multiset appear exactly once.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: for each coin c (outer): for s in c..x: dp[s] += dp[s − c]
for s in 1..x (outer): for each coin c: dp[s] += dp[s − c]
for each coin c: for s from x down to c: dp[s] += dp[s − c]
options.why: Downward iteration allows each coin type at most once.

options.text: dp[s] = Σ dp[s − c] / (number of coins)
options.why: Dividing doesn't remove duplicate orderings correctly.

extraLayers.explanation: dp[i][s] = dp[i−1][s] + dp[i][s − c_i]: either never use coin i, or use it at least once more.
